title: Strictly semistable curve
statement: Let $C,T$ be schemes and $f:C\to T$ a morphism [def-pc-scheme]. A $T$-curve is a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented morphism (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]) such that each fibre $C_t=C\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. It is strictly semistable if for every $c\in C$ there are Zariski open neighbourhoods $c\in U\subseteq C$ and $V\subseteq T$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $V$ affine, such that over $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] there is an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] from $U$ either to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] or to $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$ for some $a\in A$. The latter chart is the base change of the universal nodal chart along $a$ constructed in [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model]. No separatedness or properness is required; empty curves and empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Temkin, arXiv:0707.3953v3, section 1.2 (curve conventions), section 4.3, p. 27 (strict semistability with empty marking); primary PDF https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Stable_Modification.pdf
